We solve the inequality using the addition and multiplication principles, treating [MATH: k] like any other number.

First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting [MATH: 1] from both sides of the inequality:

[MATH: 1 − 3x|≤ 13 − 6k; 1 − 3x − 1|≤ 13 − 6k − 1; − 3x|≤ 12 − 6k]

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides of the inequality by [MATH: -3.] Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality.

[MATH: − 3x|≤ 12 − 6k; (− 3x)/((− 3))|≥ (12 − 6k)/((− 3)); x|≥ (12 − 6k)/((− 3))]

Finally, we further simplify the right-hand side, as follows:

[MATH: x|≥ (12 − 6k)/((− 3)); x|≥ (3(4 − 2k))/((− 3)); x|≥ (3(4 − 2k))/((− 3)); x|≥ (4 − 2k)/((− 1)); x|≥ 2k − 4]
